methodological_rigor.justification: The methodology is rigorous and multi-layered: a pooled CRISPR base-editing screen with 34 sgRNAs, run in two biologically independent donors and two CAR designs (1928z/19BBz), with neutral (CD19) and positive (RASA2) controls to calibrate hits. Validation spans orthogonal assays (phosphoflow, Western, scRNA-seq, Seahorse, metabolomics, 3D migration imaging) and multiple in vivo xenograft models (Nalm6 leukemia and Sh-Sy5y neuroblastoma) including tumor rechallenge for long-term persistence. Blinding of morbidity/tumor-burden operators and randomization after tumor-burden equalization are explicit; key findings are reproduced in healthy donor and heavily pretreated patient T cells. Statistical choices are largely appropriate (paired/unpaired t-tests, Shapiro-Wilk for normality, Wilcoxon for non-normal paired, Mantel-Cox for survival) with per-panel tests specified, but no adjustment for multiplicity across the many panels/markers is reported, no sample size justification is provided ("No statistical sample size was predetermined"), and several key figures rely on n=2-3 donors.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a preclinical/mechanistic study in primary human T cells, SUP-T1 line, and NSG xenograft mouse models, which maps to Oxford LoE 5. Translational relevance is strong and direct: base editing is already clinically used in CAR T cell therapies, the platform uses clinically relevant CD19, B7H3 and L1CAM CARs, and proof-of-concept is shown in T cells from heavily pretreated patients with cancer. Findings offer a deployable strategy for CAR-design-specific signaling tuning with explicit safety analyses (no malignant transformation, no CRS signature, no organ toxicity), making the translational path credible rather than speculative, though no human data are presented.

reporting_quality.justification: Methods are exhaustive for a preclinical study: reagents with catalog numbers, sgRNA sequences, editor mRNAs, electroporation parameters, cell culture details, animal housing/ethics/protocol numbers, and analysis software versions are reported, consistent with ARRIVE-style preclinical reporting. Animal randomization and partial blinding are stated; humane endpoints are defined; ethics approvals for human samples and animal work are cited. Data availability is good: three Zenodo deposits for scRNA-seq, bulk RNA-seq and metabolomics (DOIs cited), supplementary tables for antibodies and sgRNAs, and standard tool pipelines (nf-core, Scanpy, DESeq2). No explicit ARRIVE checklist is cited, sample-size justification is absent, and some methodological details (Extended Data items) are referenced but not fully self-contained in the provided text.

novelty_literature.justification: The paper articulates a specific novel concept ("ROADSTAR") - CAR-adapted base-editing of an endogenous signaling locus (PIK3CD ABD) tuned to the costimulatory domain (28z vs BBz) - and contrasts it with prior work by Schmidt et al. 2024 (Nature) and Walsh et al. 2025 (Nat Biotechnol) that screened PIK3CD variants in untransduced T cells without CAR context. The identification of opposite-direction beneficial mutations (activating E81K for BBz, attenuating L32P for 28z) and linkage of E81K to APDS-syndrome biology is a meaningful conceptual advance rather than first-in-class discovery. The contribution is a well-framed extension and combination of CAR engineering and base-editing mutagenesis rather than a wholly new mechanism, which is appropriately a strong 4 rather than 5.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly organized with a logical arc from screen design, to mechanism (signaling/transcriptomics/metabolomics), to in vivo efficacy, to CAR-design specificity, to safety. Figures are described with detailed legends including donor numbers, statistical tests, and E:T ratios, and schematics (Fig. 1a, 1h, 1j, experimental timelines) aid interpretation. Terminology is consistent (ROADSTAR, 28z/BBz), jargon is defined on first use, and the Discussion explicitly contextualizes findings against APDS literature and prior CAR-tuning work; the text is publication-ready in tone and structure.

key_strengths: CAR-adapted pooled base-editing screen with donor duplication and appropriate positive (RASA2) and neutral (CD19) sgRNA controls, identifying opposite-direction hits (E81K for BBz, L32P for 28z) that are mechanistically coherent with costimulatory biology.

Multi-modal mechanistic validation spanning phosphoflow, bulk/scRNA-seq, untargeted metabolomics, Seahorse mito-stress testing, and 3D live-cell cytotoxicity imaging, reinforcing the signaling-to-metabolism-to-function chain.
Robust in vivo efficacy demonstrated across hematological (Nalm6) and solid (Sh-Sy5y B7H3/L1CAM) tumor xenografts, including a tumor-rechallenge persistence model with long-term survival benefit.

Thorough safety package: long-term follow-up, histology, organ T cell quantification, liver enzymes, serum cytokines, and cBioPortal-based malignancy screen, directly addressing recent CAR-T secondary malignancy concerns.
Translational credibility via validation in T cells from heavily pretreated patients with sarcoma, lung and breast cancer, plus data/code deposition on Zenodo.
key_concerns: No explicit multiple-testing correction across the many pairwise comparisons in scRNA-seq cluster markers, metabolomics panels, and flow-marker panels, and no a priori sample-size justification ("No statistical sample size was predetermined").
scRNA-seq is underpowered for donor-level inference: clustering and key comparative analyses rest on one healthy donor, limiting generalizability of the transcriptional-metabolic claims.
Blinding is only partial (morbidity and tumor-burden acquisition blinded; analysis and in vitro work not blinded), and some in vivo endpoints use n=4-5 mice per group.

Safety claim rests on ~66-day follow-up in NSG mice and a cBioPortal absence-of-evidence argument; longer-term lymphomagenesis risk of an APDS-associated activating mutation cannot be excluded from the presented data.
Reporting-standard adherence is high but no formal ARRIVE checklist is cited, and several method details rely on Extended Data figures not available in the supplied text.
chief_reviewer.rationale: A methodologically strong, mechanistically deep preclinical CAR-T engineering study with novel CAR-design-specific signaling calibration, robust in vivo efficacy in both liquid and solid tumor models, explicit safety analyses, and public data deposition supports a Tier-1 ceiling (e.g., Nature Medicine / Nature Cancer scope) with minor revisions to strengthen multiplicity handling, scRNA-seq donor replication, and checklist-level reporting.
